newsitem.title: USA: First Bank Systems goes slow on Internet - CEO.
newsitem.headline: First Bank Systems goes slow on Internet - CEO.

text.p: First Bank Systems, which has often used cutting edge technology to cut costs and attract customers, will be cautious about introducing Internet services, chief executive officer John Grundhofer said Friday.
The bank will unveil its Internet-based services in the third quarter, Grundhofer said in a speech at a Chicago Federal Reserve Bank conference here.
"Nobody's making money on the web now," he said. "We're going to be very careful in terms of putting a lot of money into it before we see what the results are."

First Bank is enhancing its fee income by charging controversial "surcharges" on non-customers using the bank's automated teller machines, although less aggressively than some of its competitors, Grundhofer said.
"It is clearly a source of revenue for us that we continue to have," he said. "We are surcharging, but not to the degree that some others are."
The bank reported last month that it had record quarterly operating earnings for the first quarter of $171.8 million.
Grundhofer declined to comment on the bank's pending merger with Portland, Oregon based U.S. Bancorp.
